statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-87865: when libcurl uses the libssh2 backend for SFTP or SCP with a hashed known_hosts file, an unrelated earlier entry can make libcurl report a changed host key as a missing one to an application's CURLOPT_SSH_KEYFUNCTION callback, so a trust-on-first-use callback may accept an impostor server (https://curl.se/docs/CVE-2026-87865.html). curl's advisory says the problem only affects libcurl built with the libssh2 backend, and not the curl tool; it affects 7.69.1 to 8.22.0 and was fixed in 8.23.0 by https://github.com/curl/curl/commit/323c184b6bdf5b1988a10c0a61560666e1588149. The DHI curl packages for Alpine 3.23 published in the DHI Alpine main repository as of 2026-11-28 are builds of curl 8.17.0-r1, 8.18.0-r0, 8.19.0-r0, 8.20.0-r0, 8.20.0-r1, 8.21.0-r0, 8.22.0-r0, 8.23.0-r0 and 8.23.0-r1, and the version string in each build's libcurl matches its package version. In the libcurl, curl and curl-static packages of every one of these builds, on x86_64 and aarch64, neither libcurl.so.4 nor the curl program links libssh2, libssh or any other SSH library, and in the static libcurl.a the objects built from libssh2.c and libssh.c define no symbols, while the same check finds 50 to 56 symbols defined in the object built from openssl.c. From 8.19.0-r0 libcurl's URL scheme table lists scp and sftp, but no SSH backend is compiled to carry out such transfers. The libssh2 backend is not built, so the vulnerable code is not present. Packages published only in the DHI Alpine security repository, which needs credentials, were not inspected.

The DHI curl packages for Alpine 3.24 published in the DHI Alpine main repository as of 2026-11-28 are builds of curl 8.20.0-r1, 8.21.0-r0, 8.22.0-r0, 8.22.0-r1 and 8.23.0-r0, and the version string in each build's libcurl matches its package version. In the libcurl, curl and curl-static packages of every one of these builds, on x86_64 and aarch64, neither libcurl.so.4 nor the curl program links libssh2, libssh or any other SSH library, and in the static libcurl.a the objects built from libssh2.c and libssh.c define no symbols, while the same check finds 52 to 56 symbols defined in the object built from openssl.c. libcurl's URL scheme table lists scp and sftp, but no SSH backend is compiled to carry out such transfers. The libssh2 backend is not built, so the vulnerable code is not present. Packages published only in the DHI Alpine security repository, which needs credentials, were not inspected.
